a_records.quote: One may prove that for n = 2 the statistic 1/alpha-hat has beta distribution B(1/2, alpha) and so alpha-hat is stochastically increasing in alpha.

b_records.quote: Remark 2.3. Deriving exact distributions of the moment estimators alpha-hat and lambda-hat is tedious for n > 2. One may prove that for n = 2 the statistic 1/alpha-hat has beta distribution B(1/2, alpha) and so alpha-hat is stochastically increasing in alpha.

conclusion.direction: alpha-hat stochastically increasing in alpha (direct proof for n = 2 via beta distribution)

a_records.quote: The estimator 1/alpha-hat is not dispersively monotone in alpha.

hypotheses.text: none (negative result proved via Var(1/alpha-hat) = psi(alpha) non-monotone since lim_{alpha->0} psi = lim_{alpha->infty} psi = 0)

conclusion.direction: 1/alpha-hat is NOT dispersively monotone in alpha

a_records.ambiguity: Negative (failure) result; dispersive ordering does not hold.

b_records.quote: Theorem 2.4. The estimator 1/alpha-hat is not dispersively monotone in alpha. [Proof:] Var(1/alpha-hat) = psi(alpha) = 2 alpha (alpha+1) / ((n-1)(alpha+1/n)^2 (alpha+2/n)(alpha+3/n)); since lim_{alpha->0} psi(alpha) = lim_{alpha->inf} psi(alpha) = 0, psi is not monotone, so 1/alpha-hat cannot be dispersively monotone.

hypotheses.text: dispersive monotonicity would imply Var(1/alpha-hat) monotone in alpha

conclusion.direction: negative: 1/alpha-hat is NOT dispersively monotone in alpha
